question: What will the October 2026 US PPI for final demand (seasonally adjusted, month-over-month) be as first published by BLS?

calls.reasoning: Prior from high-inflation-regime monthly PPI prints (median ~+0.4, SD ~0.5) with post-energy-spike partial reversal. PPI pricing dates (~Sep 15 vs Oct 13): WTI ~$99-102 -> ~$95-98, Brent ~flat ~$105, RBOB ~3.3-3.5 -> ~3.17, retail gas $4.43 -> ~$4.33, implying a negative SA energy contribution (~-0.15 to -0.35pp) partly offset by seasonal factors. Core ex food/energy/trade +0.5 in Sept and ongoing pass-through support ~+0.3pp; trade services volatile (fuel margins may widen as wholesale falls; mean reversion after +1.4). Manifold P(>=0.3)=0.54 on volume 42, thin; matches terms but data descriptions inconsistent. Median ~0.2, wide tails given Sept 0.7pt consensus miss.
calls.dossier:
- BLS Sept 2026 PPI (rel. Oct 15 2026): final demand +1.3% SA m/m; energy +10.8%, gasoline +20.3%, foods +1.2%, trade services +1.4%, FD less foods/energy/trade +0.5%; May-Aug revised. Prior months per question background: Aug +0.5, Jul +0.2, Jun -0.1 (a Manifold page cites different figures: Jul 0.0, Jun -0.3, May +1.1 - inconsistent).
- PPI pricing reference is roughly the Tuesday of the week containing the 13th: ~Sep 15 vs Oct 13, 2026.
- Crude (CNBC): Sep 9 WTI $96.05/Brent $101.21; Sep 17 WTI $101.91/Brent $104.82; Oct 13 Brent close ~$105.69; Oct 15 WTI Nov $97.97, Brent Dec $105.92. Late Oct Brent ~$114, WTI ~$103 (background, after pricing date).
- RBOB (Kalkine/other): late Sept ~$3.22-3.59/gal; Oct 15 ~$3.17, falling on +3.5mb inventory build; Chicago blendstock later fell from >$4 to $3.09 (Insurance Journal Oct 29).
- AAA retail regular: Sep 3 $4.14, Sep 10 $4.27, Sep 17 $4.43, Sep 24 $4.48; Oct 8 $4.36, Oct 15 $4.33, Oct 22 $4.27, Oct 29 $4.22 (winter-blend switch).
- Seasonal adjustment normally expects gasoline declines in October, muting SA energy declines.
- Trade services (margins, ~20% weight) swing +/-1% monthly; retail fuel margins tend to widen when wholesale falls.
- Sept consensus was ~0.6 vs 1.3 actual (miss >0.5pt).
- Status quo: no change mechanism beyond monthly data; Oct CPI out Nov 10 gives partial energy/food read.
- Base rates: 2021-22 monthly PPI FD changes (over all months in that regime) median ~+0.4-0.5, SD ~0.5; months after large energy-driven spikes (e.g., Apr 2022 after Mar +1.7 -> ~+0.5; Jul 2022 after energy drop -> -0.4) show partial reversal.
- Resolves off BLS first-published Oct 2026 FD SA 1-month % change (Nov 13 release), not revisions, not core, not y/y.
- Event window: Oct 2026 reference month, published Nov 13 2026 -> as of Nov 2 2026 data month complete, release pending (~0% of uncertainty resolved publicly).
- Searched but not found: economist consensus for Oct PPI, Oct CPI (not yet out), exact Sep 15 RBOB/crude settles, diesel/jet fuel moves.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: PPI final demand prints in an energy-shock regime (2022, mid-2026). September was +1.3 with energy +10.8 and gasoline +20.3. In October, RBOB futures fell ~6% to the lowest since late August, retail gasoline was flat to slightly up (EIA, CPI preview) and CPI is expected at +0.2, so energy should be flat to negative after seasonal adjustment and could partly reverse. Upside: Brent +13-15% in October (mostly late in the month) feeding diesel, jet fuel and transport surcharges, plus firm core (+0.5 ex-FET). Trade margins after +1.4 are a wildcard either way. Manifold (thin, 5 holders) puts 54% on >=0.3. Median 0.3 with wide tails.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: PPI final demand m/m in energy-shock months (2022). A +1.3% print driven by energy has usually been followed by a much smaller print, sometimes a negative one (Mar 2022 +1.7 then Apr +0.5; Jun 2022 +1.0 then Jul -0.4). PPI prices around the Tuesday of the week containing the 13th. Mid-September was close to the crude spike (Brent about $131 on Sep 15). WTI averaged about $97 in both Sep and early Oct. Retail gasoline slipped from a $4.33 Sep average to $4.33 on Oct 15 and kept falling afterwards. So October energy is probably flat to down. Retail fuel margins fell 30% in September, and their rebound should lift trade services. Food is uncertain after +1.2%. Core is running about 0.3-0.5. Market: Manifold 'at least 0.3%' is priced at 0.54 with volume of only 42. That contract matches this one at the 0.3 threshold, but it's thin, so I treat it as weak evidence. Data sources conflict with each other (oil levels vary), so I kept the distribution wide.

calls.reasoning: Mid-Sep to mid-Oct pricing window: crude flat-to-down, RBOB and retail gasoline down (~-2%), with October seasonal factors muting the SA energy decline -> energy contributes ~-0.1 to -0.15pp. Core ex food/energy/trade running +0.3-0.5 adds ~+0.3pp. Trade margins after +1.4 are two-sided (fuel margin rebound vs mean reversion). Late-October Brent surge falls mostly after the pricing date. 2022 analogues (Mar +1.7 -> Apr +0.5; Jun +1.0 -> Jul -0.4) show sharp deceleration after energy spikes. Thin Manifold market: 54% on >=0.3, consistent.
calls.reconciliation: Runs agreed on the structure (energy flat-to-down at the pricing dates, firm core, volatile trade). Factual dispute: Sep 15 Brent level (~$131 spike per Run 3 vs ~$102-105 per Run 1). Not settleable without web access, but under either reading mid-Oct crude was not above mid-Sep, so the sign of the energy contribution holds. Retail and RBOB data across all dossiers agree gasoline fell into the Oct pricing date. The trade-margin direction is judgment; I treat it as roughly neutral to slightly positive with high variance. I carry forward Run 2/3-style dispersion and put the median at 0.25, between Run 1's energy-weighted 0.2 and Runs 2/3's 0.3, because the component arithmetic lands there, not to split the difference. No escape mass: no concrete mechanism for a print below -1.05 or above 2.55.
